claims.text: The initial material is equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr.
The intervention is application of a 10 μm thick Al2O3 ceramic coating.
The Al2O3 coating will improve the oxygen resistance of equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr.
The coating will reduce the oxidation rate by 75% relative to untreated equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr at 800 °C in air for 5 hours.
The coating will not compromise room-temperature mechanical performance.
The coating will not compromise high-temperature mechanical performance.
The Al2O3 coating acts as a barrier to oxygen diffusion.
Reduced oxygen diffusion through the coating lowers oxidation of the underlying HfNbTaTiZr alloy.
The proposed applicability boundary is 800 °C in air for 5 hours with no external loading.
The achieved oxidation-rate reduction may depend on coating thickness, uniformity, adhesion, and test conditions.
Failure to achieve at least a 50% oxidation-rate reduction relative to untreated material would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis predicts a 75% oxidation-rate reduction, but the stated rule falsifies it only below 50%; results from 50% to less than 75% would fail the quantitative prediction without falsifying the hypothesis.
